messages:
marie-docs: Heads up 11 I pushed a docs PR that adds a short EU-focused guidance section for audit log retention and encryption examples (Helm + Azure Blob / AWS). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/499

tom-ops: Nice. Can you call out differences between SOC2 recommendations and GDPR/data residency expectations? Our EU customers ask for shorter retention by default.

leah-compliance: Please avoid asserting any one-size-fits-all policy. For EU we can suggest recommended ranges and link to the compliance matrix. Wording suggestion: "Recommended retention windows vary by jurisdiction and data sensitivity; consult your compliance contact."

marie-docs: Got it. Current draft shows a values.yaml example with a 180-day example for EU, and a separate 365-day example for global defaults. Snippet: 

```
# values.yaml (examples)
audit:
  enabled: true
  retention_days: 180 # example for EU/regulatory sensitive workloads
  storage:
    provider: azure-blob
    container: "redwood-audit-eu"
  encryption:
    mode: sse-kms
    kms_key_ref: "{{ .Values.kms.key_ref }}"
```

nik-security: Please also include a short note about SSE-KMS vs client-side encryption and recommend customer-managed keys when handling regulated logs. And show how to mount a Kubernetes secret instead of embedding keys in the values file.

marie-docs: Adding a Secret example and a minimal client-side encryption call example (Python) so SREs can see both patterns: 

```
# k8s secret (example)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: audit-kms-secret
stringData:
  key_ref: "projects/myproject/locations/global/keyRings/kr/cryptoKeys/k1" # templated
```

```python
# client-side encrypt before send (illustrative)
from redwood_sdk import AuditClient
client = AuditClient()
encrypted_payload = client.encrypt_log(raw_log, kms_key=os.environ.get("KMS_REF"))
client.push_audit(encrypted_payload)
```

leah-compliance: LGTM on examples. Two phrasing asks: (1) replace any absolute terms like "must" unless it's a legal/contractual requirement, and (2) add a pointer to the compliance contact alias.

marie-docs: I'll soften wording. Also adding a short callout: "If logs contain personal data, follow local data-protection rules and consider pseudonymization before export."

tom-ops: Could we add a tiny CLI snippet showing how to set retention via the infra API? Folks copy that into automation. Something like: 

```
redwoodctl set-audit --retention 180 --region eu-west-1 --kms-ref $KMS_REF
```

nik-security: One more: include a brief note about access controls (S3/Blob ACLs, IAM roles) and retention deletion workflows (how to trigger permanent deletion) so customers understand end-to-end.

marie-docs: Adding two one-line bullets under the examples for ACLs and deletion API link. Will push updates and tag @leah-compliance @nik-security for a quick pass.

ci-bot: docs PR 499 checks: linkcheck passed, asciidoctor build OK :white_check_mark:

leah-compliance: Quick review done; I left one small suggestion to change "example for EU" to "example often used for EU-regulated logs; confirm with compliance". That keeps it advisory.

marie-docs: Updated per suggestion, removed hard-coded sample keys, added pointer to compliance alias, and merged after CI. Thanks all! :sparkles:
